"reference_description": "L1: A university enrollment system involves the following steps:
L2: Prospective students submit an application online.
L3: The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
L4: If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
L5: Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
L6: Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
L7: If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
L8: Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
L9: After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
L10: If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
L11: If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
L12: The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes:
L13: Meeting with an academic advisor.
L14: Selecting courses.
L15: Resolving any schedule conflicts.
L16: The student begins attending classes.
L17: Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
L18: At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
L19: If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes:
L20: Submitting an appeal form.
L21: Meeting with the appeals committee.
L22: Awaiting a decision.
L23: The process repeats each semester until the student graduates or withdraws.", "existing_issues": [], "semantic_view": {"processes": [{"id": "Process_1", "name": null, "nodes": [{"id": "Task_1", L3: Concurrently, the compliance team checks for any regulatory updates that might affect the audit.
L4: Afterward, the regional office submits the documents to the central audit team.
L5: The central audit team reviews the submission.
L6: If discrepancies are found, they request clarifications from the regional office.
L7: The regional office provides the necessary clarifications.
L8: Once all documents are reviewed without issues, the audit team conducts a risk assessment.
L9: The risk assessment includes evaluating financial risks, operational risks, and compliance risks, which can be done in any order but must all be completed.
L10: If high risk is identified, then a detailed investigation is launched.
L11: The investigation includes data analysis, interviews, and, in certain cases, site visits.
L12: After all risks are addressed, the audit team compiles the audit report.
L13: The report is reviewed by the audit director.
L14: The audit director may approve the report or send it back for revisions.
L15: If revisions are required, the audit team updates the report accordingly and resubmits it to be reviewed again by the audit director.
L16: Once approved, the final report is distributed to the executive board and archived.

L4: While you are setting up your account, you can already come up with good character names.

L6: If you do not have one yet, you enter the account information and click the link you receive in the confirmation mail.
L7: As soon as you have a battle.net account, you can check if you have an active WoW subscription.
L8: If not, you can select the payment method.
L9: If you choose credit card, enter your credit card information.
L10: If you choose your bank account, enter your IBAN and BIC numbers.
L11: After that you can log into the game and select realm, race and class of your character.
L12: Until now, you should have come up with some good names.
L13: You enter them one by one until a name is still available.
